To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accessory genes are essential for MV infection and pathogenesis, and that the receptor usage of measles virus in vivo is not fully understood.
we have established a reverse genetics-based monkey model of MV and have identified the receptors of MV.
the pathogenesis of MV infection is dependent on the expression of the accessory genes and on the receptor usage of the MV strain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying MV pathogenesis in vivo.
the molecular basis of the pathogenesis and the cell tropism of MV.
the elucidation of the molecular basis for cell tropism and pathogenesis of MV in monkeys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SLAM is the major receptor of wild-type MV in vivo and that nectin- 4 is an epithelial receptor for wild-type MV.
MV uses multiple receptors for infection of various cell types.
MV has a broad cell tropism in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MV infection in monkeys is useful for the study of MV pathogenesis in humans.
the pathogenicity of MV in monkeys is dependent on the receptor usage of the MV strains.
the virus tropism and pathogenesis of MV is determined by its receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of non-human primates as animal models is indispensable for the understanding of MV pathogenesis and development of effective vaccines and therapeutics.
the pathogenesis of MV infection is not determined by the viral genes but by the interaction between virus and host factors.
the reverse genetics system of wild-type MV is a powerful tool for the study of MV pathogenesis in vivo.
